chunks: From him, from Salih ibn Khalid, from Abu Jamilah, from Zayd al-Shammam, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who was a carrier (of goods) whom I hired, and I sent with him oil to Nasibin. He claimed that some of the oil skins burst and he spilled them. He said to him: 'If he wishes, he may take the oil; but if he claims that they burst, his claim is not accepted except with just evidence.'

key_terms.أَزْقَاق: Skins or bags for holding oil
key_terms.جَمَّال: Carrier or porter who transports goods

ai.seo_question: What evidence is required for a hired carrier to claim goods were damaged in transit?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the burden of proof in commercial contracts, ruling that a hired carrier's claim of accidental loss requires 'just evidence' (*bayyinah 'adilah*) rather than mere assertion. This principle safeguards the owner against false claims by establishing a high evidentiary standard for liability exemption, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on fairness (*'adl*) in financial transactions.
